+# Contentful Developer Guide
+
+A draft guide for working with Contentful on the Zimmermann PWA.
+
+---
+
+## What Contentful is for
+
+We use Contentful as the CMS for editorial content — homepage, banners, footer, campaign pages, and other marketing content.
+
+Commerce data (products, prices, orders) comes from SFCC.
+
+---
+
+## Concepts worth knowing upfront
+
+**Space** = the Zimmermann Contentful account. There is one shared space across all environments.
+
+**Environments** = isolated copies of the content schema and data within the space, e.g. `dev`, `test`, `master` (production). Your local dev server points at whichever environment is set in your `.env`.
+
+**Content type** = a schema (like a database table). Examples: `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`, etc. Defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed via `npm run sync:contentful`.
+
+**Experiences** — Contentful Studio's visual page-builder feature. An Experience is a page (e.g. the homepage) where an editor can drag and drop registered React components. Experiences are different to regular content entries — they have their own WYSIWYG editor in the Contentful UI.
+
+---
+
+## Setting up your local environment
+
+### 1. Get your personal management token
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your avatar (top right) → Account settings → [CMA tokens](app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens) → Create personal access token**. Give it a name like "My dev token" and set an expiry. Click **Generate**, then copy the token immediately — you will not see it again.
+
+Add it to your `.env` file (not `.env.sample`):
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN=your-token-here
+```
+
+This token is personal — never commit or share it.
+
+### 2. Populate the rest of the Contentful env vars
+
+With your management token in `.env`, run:
+
+```bash
+npm run config:contentful
+```
+
+This fetches the delivery token, preview token, and environment ID from the live Contentful space and writes them into your `.env`. You only need to run this once (or again after rotating your management token).
+
+### 3. Point at the dev environment for local work
+
+After running `config:contentful`, check that your `.env` has:
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=dev
+```
+
+The default fetched value may be `master` (production). Switch it to `dev` for local development so you are not reading from or writing to live production content.
+
+---
+
+## Testing Contentful content locally
+
+When the local dev server is running (`npm start`), the PWA reads from the Contentful environment set in your `.env`.
+
+To connect Contentful's web editor to your local dev server so you can preview content changes live:
+
+1. Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Settings → Content preview → Create preview platform**.
+2. Fill in the fields:
+   - **Name:** something like "Zimmermann localhost"
+   - **Preview URL for Experiences:** `http://localhost:3000/{entry.fields.slug}`  
+     (To preview against the dev environment instead of localhost, use: `https://zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com/{entry.fields.slug}`)
+3. Go to **Experiences**, open an existing Experience (or create a new one).
+4. In the **Settings** tab on the left of the Experience editor, select the preview platform you just created (e.g. Zimmermann localhost).
+
+Changes you make in the Experience editor will now hot-reload in your browser.
+
+---
+
+## Browsing and creating content
+
+### Finding content types
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Content model**. This shows all available content types for Zimmermann (e.g. `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`).
+
+### Adding or changing a content type schema
+
+> **Don't confuse these two things:**
+>
+> - The `generate:contentful` script (and pre-commit hook) handles the **Experiences component registry** — it controls which React components appear in the Studio canvas. It only reads your source files; it never calls the Contentful API.
+> - `sync:contentful` (below) handles **content type schemas** — the field definitions pushed to the Contentful API. These are separate.
+>
+> A component like the test `ShoppableImage` has both: a content type schema (so editors can create ShoppableImage entries) and an Experiences registration (so it appears in the drag-and-drop canvas). They're maintained separately.
+
+**Content type schemas** are defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed to Contentful with:
+
+```bash
+npm run sync:contentful
+```
+
+This is for schema changes (adding/removing content type fields), not for creating content entries. It requires your `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Always run against a non-production environment first — the sync is additive-only and **cannot delete fields from a published content type**, so a mistaken field push to production is hard to undo.
+
+### Adding a content entry
+
+1. Go to **Content → Add entry** and pick a content type (e.g. PLP).
+2. Fill in the fields.
+3. Click **Publish**.
+
+The entry is now available via the Contentful Delivery API. On the PWA side, entries are queried by content type using the `useContentfulEntries` hook:
+
+```tsx
+import { useContentfulEntries } from '../../hooks/useContentful';
+
+// Fetches all entries of the 'plp' content type (e.g. hero banner, promo content)
+const { data, isLoading, error } = useContentfulEntries<PlpEntry>('plp');
+
+// data = PLP entries (if there are multiple) ordered by creation date
+const entry = data?.[0];
+```
+
+(Using that as an example because in PLP, the product list would come from SFCC, but editorial content (hero banner, promotional image/copy) comes from Contentful alongside it via this hook.)
+
+### Creating an Experience page
+
+Pages that are fully content-managed (like the home page and campaign/collection pages) use **Contentful Studio Experiences** (the WYSIWYG). The homepage is planned to be an Experience (the whole page laid out in Contentful Studio). While things like parts of the PLP, the footer, and the announcement banner/bar are regular content entries with editorial fields alongside their SFCC data.
+
+1. Go to **Experiences → Add experience**.
+2. Fill in:
+   - **Title:** your page name
+   - **Slug:** the URL path, e.g. `summer` makes the page live at `localhost:3000/summer` or `zimmermann.com/summer`
+3. Drag and drop registered components into the page canvas.
+4. Click **Publish** when ready.
+
+---
+
+## Registering a React component with Contentful
+
+To make a React component available in the Contentful Studio drag-and-drop canvas, it needs to be registered. Here is the full process:
+
+### 1. Place the component in the right folder
+
+Registerable components currently live in:
+
+```
+overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/
+```
+
+If you want to expose an existing component (e.g. `ProductCard`) to Contentful, create a thin wrapper in that folder rather than adding `@cf` tags to the original. The wrapper lets you deliberately limit which props editors can see and change them to be more editor-friendly, without touching the core component's interface:
+
+```tsx
+// overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/productCardCf.tsx
+import ProductCard from '../../productCard';
+
+type ProductCardCfProps = {
+  /** @cf Product ID */
+  productId: string;
+  /** @cf Show quick-add button, boolean */
+  showQuickAdd: boolean;
+};
+
+/** @cf-register */
+const ProductCardCf = ({ productId, showQuickAdd }: ProductCardCfProps) => (
+  <ProductCard id={productId} enableQuickAdd={showQuickAdd} />
+);
+
+export default ProductCardCf;
+```
+
+Internal props like `isLoading`, `onAddToCart`, or complex object shapes stay invisible to editors — only what you explicitly declare in the wrapper's `Props` type appears in the Contentful sidebar.
+
+### 2. Run the registration skill
+
+Run the `/contentful-register-component` Claude skill. It will:
+
+- Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before your component's `const` declaration — this opts it in to the code generator
+- Add `/** @cf Display Name */` JSDoc comments to each prop in your `Props` type — these tell Contentful what label and control to show in the editor sidebar
+
+### 3. The `@cf` tag syntax
+
+Each prop annotation follows this pattern:
+
+```ts
+type MyComponentProps = {
+  /** @cf Headline */
+  headline: string;
+
+  /** @cf Body Text, longText */
+  body: string;
+
+  /** @cf Layout, select */
+  imagePosition: 'left' | 'right';
+
+  /** @cf Background Image, media */
+  backgroundImage: ContentfulAsset;

+# Contentful Developer Guide
+
+A draft guide for working with Contentful on the Zimmermann PWA.
+
+---
+
+## What Contentful is for
+
+We use Contentful as the CMS for editorial content — homepage, banners, footer, campaign pages, and other marketing content.
+
+Commerce data (products, prices, orders) comes from SFCC.
+
+---
+
+## Concepts worth knowing upfront
+
+**Space** = the Zimmermann Contentful account. There is one shared space across all environments.
+
+**Environments** = isolated copies of the content schema and data within the space, e.g. `dev`, `test`, `master` (production). Your local dev server points at whichever environment is set in your `.env`.
+
+**Content type** = a schema (like a database table). Examples: `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`, etc. Defined in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` and pushed via `npm run sync:contentful`.
+
+**Experiences** — Contentful Studio's visual page-builder feature. An Experience is a page (e.g. the homepage) where an editor can drag and drop registered React components. Experiences are different to regular content entries — they have their own WYSIWYG editor in the Contentful UI.
+
+---
+
+## Setting up your local environment
+
+### 1. Get your personal management token
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your avatar (top right) → Account settings → [CMA tokens](app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens) → Create personal access token**. +
+Add it to your `.env` file (not `.env.sample`):
+
+```
+CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN=your-token-here
+```
+
+This token is personal — never commit or share it.
+
+### 2. Populate the rest of the Contentful env vars
+
+With your management token in `.env`, run:
+
+```bash
+npm run config:contentful
+```

+This fetches the delivery token, preview token, and environment ID from the live Contentful space and writes them into your `.env`. You only need to run this once (or again after rotating your management token).
+
+### 3. Point at the dev environment for local work

+CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=dev
+```

+
+---

+   - **Preview URL for Experiences:** `http://localhost:3000/{entry.fields.slug}`

+4. In the **Settings** tab on the left of the Experience editor, select the preview platform you just created (e.g. Zimmermann localhost).

+Changes you make in the Experience editor will now hot-reload in your browser.
+
+---

+## Browsing and creating content

+### Finding content types
+
+Go to **app.contentful.com → your Space → Content model**. This shows all available content types for Zimmermann (e.g. `plp`, `topBanner`, `footer`).

+### Adding or changing a content type schema

+>
+> - The `generate:contentful` script (and pre-commit hook) handles the **Experiences component registry** — it controls which React components appear in the Studio canvas. It only reads your source files; it never calls the Contentful API.

=== pre-commit hook (derived-file blocking) ===
#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
#
# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
  # nvm (most common on macOS)
  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

  # fnm
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi

  # volta
  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
  fi

  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi

/**
 * Sync .cursor/rules/, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and .vscode/instructions/

 *   node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs          # report drift
 *   node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --check  # exit 1 if any drift found (CI mode)
 *   node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix    # regenerate auto-generated rules
 */

import fs from 'fs'
import path from 'path'
import {fileURLToPath} from 'url'

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..')

    'overrides/app/pages/cart/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/checkout/**',
    'overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/**',

# 02 — Contentful (CMS)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.

In scope:

- Reading published content via the Delivery API
- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
- Live preview in Contentful Studio
- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries

Out of scope of this document:

- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
